source: Uzair, chat 2026-10-09: curated list for #causal-discovery ('CD Tracker'); anything not named is excluded (REP-10 and categories INF, CRS, TEAM, EXT, STR, DEC, RSK). Quarter 1 deliverables DLV-01..06 added on his request.

rows.title: Replicate Causal-Copilot paper claims and results
rows.criterion: Each headline claim and result of the Causal-Copilot paper, and the external results about it, marked reproduced, not reproducible (with the reason) or not attempted.

rows.title: Replicate CausalArena baselines
rows.criterion: CausalArena's published baselines reproduced with our scorer, within tolerance or with the gap explained.

rows.title: Replicate Causal Chambers baselines
Literature mapping
rows.criterion: Literature, benchmarks, nearest prior work and the wider landscape mapped, every second-hand claim checked against its source.

rows.title: Theoretical baselines
rows.criterion: The theory the work rests on (identifiability, finite samples, calibration, interventions, hidden causes, scale) written down, with the methods chosen.

rows.title: Architecture mapping
rows.criterion: How Causal-Copilot is built and what each step does to the graph, measured from recorded runs.

rows.title: Causal-Copilot on CausalArena's named scenarios
rows.criterion: Causal-Copilot audited on CausalArena's named scenarios under name and column controls, with the benchmark itself audited first.

rows.title: Targets from evidence
rows.criterion: Every target derived from measured evidence, with its source and the information regime it applies to.

rows.title: Does the LLM review write edges from the variable names rather than the data, and does the bootstrap step delete undirected edges? (Sachs, pass 4b P1-P3: supported)
With neutral names, does the LLM write at most half as many edges as with real names? (bundle 1 N2: supported)
On four more datasets, do moved names steer the LLM's edges, does refinement lower adjacency F1, and does the bootstrap step drop most undirected edges? (bundle 1 N1, N4, P3: inconclusive)
Does the source of a method's order information explain most of its directed-edge accuracy on public benchmarks?
Do deployed agents take edge directions from names and column layout rather than from the numbers?

Can a system that holds order as a typed, sourced partial order stay at or above its own data-only output, be only boundedly harmed by wrong knowledge, and reach the best published number in each information regime?
Can every claim carry calibrated confidence and a machine-checkable derivation, so that the system can decline to claim?
Can the graph answer 'what happens if we set X?' with a stated identification status, verified on held-out interventions?
Can the system pick the experiment that settles the most open directions, better than random on recorded real experiments?
With real names, does a model's ordering of variables get at least 70% of true edges right and contradict at most 10%?
With neutral names, does the model supply no order information at all?
With names moved onto other columns, does the model's ordering follow the labels instead of the data?
Does regression on the model's ordering reach the best published 0.634 on CausalArena's semantic family with columns shuffled?
Does the same reach the best published 0.524 on the formula family?
